parsed.explanation: The combined regime is high risk. National passport/entry rules force birth-sex markers and allow refusal or fraud findings when presentation contradicts records; federal custody and government-funded facility restrictions are severe and traveller-facing. State courts block several enacted local restrictions, so local bathrooms, K-12 facilities, youth care and marker rules are materially safer than the parent average; ordinances and equal-protection rulings provide some recourse. But these local protections do not displace border screening, federal buildings/funding, immigration/federal custody, or national hostility to minor care. Adult-alone exposure centres on entry/federal facilities/custody; travelling with a minor adds unresolved national child-care/school investigations. Local violence data is absent, which is uncertainty, not safety. Net slightly below 0.35 anchors due federal border/custody exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports require M/F at birth; X markers stopped. Entry screening can refuse, demand evidence, and pursue fraud/permanent ineligibility when records conflict; travellers report passports blocked or confiscated.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; national court suits and legal-aid FAQs exist. State courts block local marker hostility but cannot change national border rules.
entry_documents.interaction: A border discrepancy can escalate into immigration custody or denial; federal screening operates irrespective of state equal-protection rulings.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections/immigration custody reports: removal of hormone medication, conversion-therapy-like measures, forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse. Document mismatch may trigger detention.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented for state custody. National litigation and legal-aid may help, but no local remedy displaces federal placement.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border/federal investigation can feed custody; state protective rulings are irrelevant to federal detention conditions.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars gender-congruent use of government-funded single-sex facilities; many other jurisdictions criminalise or exclude. Federal buildings and programs still pose risk.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State facilities bill is temporarily restrained; a 2024 proposal failed; local ordinances/municipal protections may aid. State public buildings may be safer if restraint holds.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local injunctions do not pre-empt federal facilities or funding conditions; traveller may pass through both systems.

care_services.exposure: National rules freeze funding, threaten reimbursement, criminalise school facilitation, and subpoena hospital records for youth care; adult visitor care not documented.
care_services.protection: State minor care ban permanently struck; state highest court keeps privacy protections; some local services may continue.
care_services.interaction: Family care requests or school transitions can interact with federal investigations and national funding conditions, not just state law.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National hostility frames gender identity as ideology and links advocacy to security threats; flag ban and drag bill in state show hostile legislative culture.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State courts repeatedly block anti-trans laws as animus/sex discrimination and affirm dignity; national hate-crime statute and some local ordinances apply.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State rule of law lowers local street/service risk, but federal agencies and border officers still enforce hostile national rules.

minors_guardians.exposure: Adult travelling with trans or gender-nonconforming minor may encounter national child-care/school criminalization, records scrutiny, and care interruption; unresolved federal rules.
minors_guardians.protection: State youth care ban struck and facility/marker restrictions blocked; marriage/adoption climate supportive; courts emphasize dignity.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's care or school needs can trigger federal child-protection/funding exposure even when state law is protective.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific anti-trans violence, count, or policing pattern is documented; national data are partial and not jurisdiction-specific.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute applies, but state statute lacks gender identity; local municipal protections and functioning courts are indirect only.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Without local incident data, cannot infer frequent street targeting or safety; if violence occurs, state courts may offer recourse better than many jurisdictions.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Key federal and state injunctions remain provisional; facilities TRO and marker litigation may lapse; passport rules already in force; traveller remedy uncertain and slow.
remedies_unknowns.protection: State appellate courts upheld injunctions; legal-aid FAQ provides documentation advice; some state ordinances exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Outcomes depend on timing and whether encounter is state or federal; federal enforcement can bypass local protections.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has a nationwide public-building birth-sex rule with no exemption. This state's local facilities and care restrictions are blocked, improving ordinary service exposure. But national passport/entry rules and federal custody abuse create border/custody severity absent from 0.35-A. Net slightly below because federal exposure follows the traveller and lacks local remedy.

0.25-D has compulsory birth-sex facilities/hospitals and police fraud stops in the destination state itself. Here the state's own facility/care rules are restrained by courts, so local exposure is lower. The federal border/fraud and custody layer keeps the rating well below 0.45 but above 0.25-D.

0.45-D features invasive national transport searches with recurring complaints and some bias prosecutions, but no state-level passport/care hostility. Here entry screening can deny/fraud, federal custody abuse is documented, and national minor-care hostility exists, while local courts only partially mitigate. This places it below 0.45-D.

parsed.synthesis: National rules create a tier-one journey: passport/marker mismatch can trigger denial, additional evidence, immigration detention, and harsh federal custody; government-funded facilities may exclude. Local courts neutralize the worst state statutes: no operative bathroom/care ban, injunctions on marker and school rules, and equal-protection dignity rulings. This raises the state above many subnational divisions and above the parent average, but cannot override federal screening, federal custody, or national child-care hostility. Minors and families face additional care/school uncertainty. Absent local violence figures, the score follows the documented federal exposure and its only partially effective state remedy.
